questions.question_text: Where must a Utah principal broker maintain the brokerage trust account?
questions.correct_answer: A bank or credit union located in Utah
distractors: Any bank located in any state
The Division of Real Estate office
Any federally insured institution, in or out of state
questions.explanation: A principal broker must keep at least one real estate trust account in a bank or credit union located within Utah, and must notify the Division in writing of the account number, the institution's address, and the activity the account is used for (R162-2f-403a(1)). The account is non-interest-bearing unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

questions.question_text: A principal broker deposits $50 of personal funds into the trust account to cover monthly bank service charges. This is:
distractors: Prohibited as commingling of any amount
Only allowed with Division approval
Permitted only up to $100
questions.explanation: A principal broker may keep a modest amount of the broker's own funds in the trust account for bank charges. Utah sets the line at $1,000: depositing more than $1,000 of the broker's own funds into a real estate trust account violates 61-2f-401(4)(b) (R162-2f-403a(13)). The property management trust account limit is $10,000.

questions.question_text: Which funds may a Utah principal broker NOT deposit into a trust account?
questions.correct_answer: Money from tourist accommodation rentals of under 30 days
distractors: Earnest money on a purchase contract
Tenant security deposits
Rent collected for a managed property
questions.explanation: Funds from the rental of tourist accommodations for periods of less than 30 consecutive days may not go into either trust account (R162-2f-403a(3), 403b(3)). Earnest money, security deposits, and rent are trust funds that do belong in the appropriate trust account.

questions.question_text: A sales agent collects a $3,000 earnest money check from a buyer. The agent should:
questions.correct_answer: Deliver it to the principal broker for deposit within three business days
distractors: Deposit it in their own account
Hold it until the inspection period ends
Return it to the buyer for safekeeping
questions.explanation: The principal broker must deposit client money into a trust account within three business days of receipt, unless the contract states the money is held for a set time or deposited on acceptance (R162-2f-401c(1)(h)(i)). Sales agents never hold or deposit trust funds themselves.

questions.question_text: A broker uses $2,000 from the trust account to pay their office rent. This is an example of:
distractors: Proper fund management
Commingling of accounts
An authorized business expense
questions.explanation: Using trust money for the broker's own purposes is conversion — diverting money from the purpose for which it was received, prohibited by 61-2f-401(4)(c). It is more serious than commingling and supports revocation.

questions.question_text: Which documents must a Utah broker retain for Division inspection?
questions.correct_answer: Contracts, closing statements, and trust ledgers
distractors: Only signed purchase contracts
Only trust account bank statements
Only documents from the last 6 months
questions.explanation: The principal broker must keep trust account records including the monthly reconciliation, documents submitted to a lender or underwriter, documents the parties jointly execute where an agency agreement is required, and documents executed by supervised licensees (R162-2f-401k(1)).

questions.question_text: The Division contacts a broker requesting transaction records for review. The broker must:
questions.correct_answer: Make all records available for inspection
distractors: Provide records only with a court subpoena
Allow review of trust accounts only
Schedule the review at least 60 days out
questions.explanation: Records must be made available for Division inspection and copying on request (R162-2f-401k(3)), and failing to respond within 10 business days is itself grounds for discipline (61-2f-401(18)). No subpoena or court order is needed.

questions.question_text: A broker terminates business operations but still holds transaction records. The broker must:
questions.correct_answer: Notify the Division in writing within 10 business days where the records will be kept
distractors: Destroy all records immediately
Transfer the records to the Association of REALTORS
Return all records to the clients involved
questions.explanation: Written notice must reach the Division within 10 business days after terminating business operations, stating where the records will be maintained (R162-2f-401k(4)). Records must still be kept for at least three calendar years after the year the transaction closes or fails, an offer is rejected, a lease commences, or a management agreement ends (61-2f-309).

questions.question_text: A broker discovers that correspondence related to a transaction was accidentally deleted from their records. The broker should:
questions.correct_answer: Attempt to reconstruct and retain the records
distractors: Report the deletion to the police
Ignore it since the transaction is closed
File a complaint against themselves
questions.explanation: Records must be complete and available for the Division (R162-2f-401k). A brokerage that cannot produce required records risks discipline under 61-2f-401(9), so the broker should reconstruct what was lost and document the effort.

questions.question_text: Trust account ledgers must show all of the following EXCEPT:
distractors: Deposits received and dates
Disbursements made and dates
Running balance of trust funds
questions.explanation: Deposit records must show the transaction number or client identifier, payor and payee, amount, property location, and date and place of deposit, with a running balance and monthly reconciliation against both bank and client records (R162-2f-403a(4), (10)). The broker's own operating balance has no place there.

questions.question_text: Who is responsible for supervising activities at a brokerage branch office in Utah?
distractors: The branch office manager only
Each individual sales agent
The Real Estate Commission
questions.explanation: The principal broker must exercise active and reasonable supervision (61-2f-206(5)), and although a branch broker may be designated to supervise a branch (61-2f-206(6)), the principal broker stays personally responsible and accountable (R162-2f-401c(1)(k)).

questions.question_text: A brokerage opens a new branch office across town. What must happen?
questions.correct_answer: The branch office must be registered with the Division
distractors: The branch must obtain a separate brokerage license
The branch must have its own principal broker
The branch must operate under a different business name
questions.explanation: A principal broker must register each branch office with the Division (61-2f-206(2)(a)), and the application must identify the branch broker, the physical address, the licensees assigned there, and each trust account used at that location (R162-2f-205(3)(c)).

questions.question_text: A principal broker has three branch offices. A sales agent at one branch commits a trust account violation. The PB is:
questions.correct_answer: Responsible for the violation as supervisor
distractors: Not liable since they were at another office
Only liable if they directly participated
Responsible only if there was a complaint
questions.explanation: The principal broker remains personally responsible and accountable for supervising every affiliated licensee and every branch (R162-2f-401c(1)(k)), and a failure to supervise is an independent violation under 61-2f-401(13).

questions.question_text: Which statement about Utah branch offices is correct?
questions.correct_answer: Each branch is registered with the Division under the same business name
distractors: Each branch needs its own brokerage license
Branches must be in different counties
Branches cannot handle trust funds
questions.explanation: Branch offices operate under the principal broker's brokerage but must be separately registered (61-2f-206(2)), and R162-2f-205(4)(b) requires a branch to operate under the same business name as the principal brokerage.

questions.question_text: Which location may a Utah brokerage use without registering it as a branch office?
questions.correct_answer: A model home or project sales office
distractors: A second full-time office in another city
Any office staffed by a branch broker
A permanent office with its own trust account
questions.explanation: Real estate business may be conducted at a model home, a project sales office, or a facility established for 12 months or less as a temporary marketing site — such as an exhibit booth — without branch registration (R162-2f-205(2)). Any other additional office must be registered.
